data.name: Manuan
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name 'Menachem' meaning 'consolation', 'Manuan' can be interpreted as 'God is man'. In the Old Testament, Menachem was a king of Israel who brought comfort to his people. In the New Testament, the name can be seen as a reminder of God's presence among us as human beings.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of God's presence and divine intervention in human life.
data.numerology_meaning: Manuan is a name that resonates with the vibration of the number 2 in numerology. This number is associated with balance, harmony, and partnership. People with this name are often peacemakers, mediators, and diplomats. They have a natural ability to bring people together and create harmony in any situation. They are also highly sensitive and intuitive, with a strong inner sense of what is right and fair.

in_hebrew.name: מנואן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם מנואן נגזר מהשורשים העבריים 'מנה' ו'אל', ומשמעותו 'מתנת אלוהים' או 'משיחו של האל'. השם מופיע בשורשים עבריים ומעיד על קשר ישיר לאלוהים, כמתנה או כמשיח.

in_greek.name: Μανουάν
in_greek.meaning: Δωρεὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ, Χριστός τοῦ Θεοῦ
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Μανουάν ἐκ τῶν Ἑβραϊκῶν ῥιζῶν 'Μαν' καὶ 'Αλ', καὶ σημαίνει 'Δωρεὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ' ἤ 'Χριστός τοῦ Θεοῦ'. Ἐμφανίζεται εἰς τὰ Ἑβραϊκά ῥίζα καὶ μαρτυρεῖ περὶ σχέσεως πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν, ὡς δωρεὰ ἤ Χριστός.

in_latin.name: Manuan
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Manuan ex radicibus Hebraicis 'Man' et 'Al' derivatur, et significat 'Donum Dei' vel 'Christus Domini'. Apparetur in radicibus Hebraicis et testificatur de connexione directa ad Deum, ut donum vel Christus.

historical_references.reference: Manuan, a native chief of Luzon, who submitted to Spanish rule in 1574, became a Christian and was named 'Don Alonso Manuan'. He was later appointed as the 'gobernador' of the town of Tanza in Cavite province.

Manuan, a Tagalog prince of Bukidnon, southern Philippines, who embraced Christianity in the late 17th century. He is best known for his role in the spread of Christianity in the region and was a significant ally for the Spanish missionaries.
